thread:
katie: Follow-up from yesterday's RFC sync: I'm proposing a "minimal-handshake" relay that lives in customer VPCs. Purpose: terminate short-lived mTLS to our controlplane, surface only auth+health+optional srcip hints. Keep lifecycle management centralized.

diego: can you define "minimal" concretely? we need to know operational surface were committing to.

katie: minimal = two listener ports (controlplane mTLS + admin), <1 MB on-disk, no kernel-level changes, single binary, config via env or file. state: only ephemeral CSR cache + tiny prefix cache (max 8k entries).

anita: source-ip preservation is the big ask from customers. options?

katie: two modes: app-propagation (relay attaches X-Rd-Src header over mTLS, used for billing/geo) and hairpin-egress (we provision per-customer egress ips and hairpin NAT back into our regional relays). hairpin is only for contracted customers due to IP + routing costs.

oleh: header propagation is easy but risk of header spoofing. how will we prove authenticity to downstream services?

katie: every mTLS session binds to a short cert issued by our CA; we stamp a request-id and signature on src-hint header. downstream services can verify signature using our public certs. we'll document verification libs.

infra-bot: rollout: minimal-handshake v0.1 deployed to canary cohort (2 customers) at 14:12 UTC, health checks passing :white_check_mark:

diego: what's the auth bootstrap? we must avoid customer-maintained secrets that never rotate.

katie: CSR-based flow: customer creates a scoped bootstrap token via Console -> slim-relay uses token to request CSR approval -> CP issues short-lived cert (5m default) -> relay renews via jittered backoff. sequence: 1) create bootstrap-token 2) relay posts CSR 3) CP validates token + CA issues small cert.

courtney: CA QPS concern: with thousands of relays onboarding, churn could K.O. CA. mitigation?

katie: CA autoscaling + write-through token bucket + 2-stage bootstrap (pre-approve tokens for fastpath). also relays will cache certs briefly and use retry windows. well add a per-org throttle to Console.

anita: failure/fallback semantics? if a local relay drops, what's the exact path?

katie: fallback policy chain (configurable): 1) local-relay (preferred) 2) regional-shared-relay (our infra inside customer region) 3) global-hosted-fallback (public CP). Fallback rules are observable and traceable. Default alerts if traffic falls back > 5% for 10m.

diego: observability: what metrics + logs do we expose?

katie: metrics: relay.p50_latency_ms, relay.p95_latency_ms, relay.fallback_ratio, relay.cert_renew_failures, relay.src_hint_mode (enum). Logs: structured events for CSR lifecycle, fallback events, and src-hint signature verification failures. We'll ship dashboards in Redwood Console.

oleh: perf: will relay do any L7 transformations (batching, KV caching)?

katie: minimal KV prefix cache only (for handshake tokens and small prefixes), ttl default 300s. batching/inference-level caching is explicitly disabled in minimal-handshake; well offer a separate "augmented-relay" variant for customers who opt into L7 features.

courtney: security playbook: revocation, compromise detection, and forced shutdown?

katie: controlplane will support push-based revocation message (signed), regional relays sync revocation markers. relays will accept revocation and self-terminate within jittered 60-300s window. Console has an emergency kill option which triggers immediate revocation and network ACL change.

anita: testing checklist before wider rollout?

katie: canary -> dark-traffic -> opt-in beta -> ramp. Gate thresholds: rollback if >1.5% 5xx increase, >25ms p50 degradation, or >7% fallback rate. We'll run source-ip preservation test suite, verification of header signature, and simulated CA spike.

diego: add an opt-in eBPF tracer to help debug src-ip pathing. must be disabled by default.

katie: agreed, opt-in only, will include strict RBAC.

infra-bot: note: perf test scheduled 2025-06-07 03:00 UTC.

katie: I'll draft the RFC follow-up with sequence diagrams, threat model appendix, and the rollout runbook. Thanks for the quick feedback everyone. :raised_hands:
